correctness.rationale: The two symmetric weighted 4x4 adjacency matrices have exact characteristic-polynomial difference P_A(x,t)-P_B(x,t)=-tx[(alpha^2-beta^2)tx+2b(a alpha-c beta)]. Deleting row/column 3 of A gives principal spectrum {a,0,-a}, so by interlacing its second eigenvalue is <=a; the B Perron eigenvalue is >a. Thus evaluating the A polynomial at lambda_B has exactly the sign of lambda_B-lambda_A. The sign rule follows for every positive parameter. Since lambda_B(t) strictly increases and t lambda_B(t) runs from zero to infinity, there is exactly one positive crossing iff (alpha^2-beta^2)(a alpha-c beta)<0; all ties and fixed-sign boundaries follow. Independent SymPy checks verified the determinant identity and algebraic sample crossing; numerical tests do not replace the Perron-interlacing proof.
